summary.text: Cameron Miller is the Democratic candidate for the Nevada State Assembly, District 7, in the November 3, 2026 general election; he previously represented the district in the Assembly from 2020 to 2023.
Miller is a producer whose career includes serving as chief operating officer of Studio 11 Films and hosting a Nevada public affairs talk show.

paragraphs.text: Cameron Miller was born in Las Vegas and graduated from Southeast Career Technical Academy.
He earned a B.A. in ministry leadership from Northwest University.
Ballotpedia lists his career experience as chief operating officer of Studio 11 Films, host of a Nevada public affairs talk show, and executive producer for film and television.

Miller won the Democratic primary for Nevada State Assembly District 7 in June 2020 and the general election that November over Republican Anthony Palmer, and he took office on November 4, 2020, succeeding Dina Neal.
He was re-elected in 2022 with 63.5% of the vote and left office on October 20, 2023, and Tanya Flanagan succeeded him.

During his time in the Assembly he served on the Growth and Infrastructure, Judiciary and Revenue committees in 2021-2022, and on the Growth and Infrastructure, Legislative Operations and Elections, and Ways and Means committees in 2023-2024.
Miller ran for Las Vegas City Council Ward 5 in 2024 in a nonpartisan race and lost to Shondra Summers-Armstrong, 53.5% to 46.5%.
He advanced from the canceled June 9, 2026 Democratic primary for Assembly District 7 without appearing on the ballot.
